summary: Red-flashing light on the east breakwater at Two Harbors, Minnesota: lantern lit 1895, gas light 1902, iron tower 1906, removed 1947 and re-established 1950.

corrections.why: Lighthouse Friends quotes the Light-House Board that the combined light and fog-bell tower was completed on 4 August 1906. The station record's 1897 comes from Wikidata/Rowlett, which were not read; no source read supports 1897 for the tower. The USLHS record gives 'Year Tower Established: 1895' and 'Tower Construction Material: Steel', which Lighthouse Friends does not mention. The story states the 1906 and 1895 dates as a disagreement. Human review needed.

The Light List, Volume VII (2025), entry LLNR 16505, gives the range as 9 in its range column. The entry name and 'Fl R 6s' pass check_quotes against the cached navcen PDF; the range value is read from the same row, not quote-checked. Human review needed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive's field 'Active Aid to Navigation? No' conflicts with the 2025 Light List (active, entry LLNR 16505) and with Lighthouse Friends ('remains in service today'). Resolved in favour of active; the archive field appears stale.

notes_for_editor: Thin station. (1) No keeper is named for the breakwater light in the archive or in Lighthouse Friends, and none is named in any source I read, so the keepers chapter is left out. The land Two Harbors Lighthouse (record us-mn-two-harbors) had its own keepers; the story does not attribute them to the breakwater. (2) No storm, wreck or rescue is tied to the breakwater light in the sources I read; the Storms chapter is left out. (3) The 1902 move and 1906 tower come from Lighthouse Friends, which quotes Light-House Board reports for those years; the corpus holds Light-House Board reports only to 1901, so those are secondary here. The 1906 quotation is checked against the Lighthouse Friends cache. (4) First post position: Lighthouse Friends says 'on the outer end of the eastern breakwater' for 1895; the 1896 report says 'on the west end of the breakwater'. The story reports both. (5) Focal height: the 1906 Board figure quoted by Lighthouse Friends is 33 1/2 feet to the focal plane; the archive gives 29 feet above mean high water; the station record's 9.8 m (32 ft) has no source read here and is not used. (6) The 2025 Light List (navcen PDF, cached) passes check_quotes for the entry name and 'Fl R 6s'; the range of 9 is read from the same row of the cached text and is not a quoted claim. The local copy is data/raw/uscg_light_list/V7.txt. The same list shows the west breakwater light (LLNR 16515, Fl G 4s on a post); the story does not describe its current state. (7) Lighthouse Friends gives VHF channel 79 for the fog signal; the Light List gives 83A. Not used. (8) Duplicate record: data/stations/mn/us-mn-two-harbors-east-breakwater.json (status inactive, no structures) appears to describe this same light. Merge is for a human. (9) One Chronicling America search (Minnesota, Two Harbors breakwater lighthouse, 1893-1930) returned no relevant page text; the Cook County Herald of 16 November 1907, p. 5, is a possible lead I did not read. (10) Wikipedia's lead says the light was discontinued 1947-1950 and that the tower is from 1906; it is not cited. (11) Confidence: low, because the breakwater light has few primary sources of its own. (12) Tower date and material: Lighthouse Friends gives 1906 and iron (quoting the Board); the archive gives 'Year Tower Established: 1895' and steel. The story states both and does not choose. (13) Active aid: the archive says 'Active Aid to Navigation? No'; Lighthouse Friends says the light 'remains in service today' and the 2025 Light List has it as Fl R 6s. The story gives the archive's 'No' next to the Light List entry. (14) The Commissioner's 1916 list was checked in the volume: 'Two Harbors Breakwater, Minn.' sits under 'ELECTRIC INCANDESCENT LIGHTS (73 LIGHTS)' in the list 'in Commission on June 30, 1916' (scan p. 145). The 1917 west breakwater entry is in the aids-established narrative (scan p. 216). Scan pages were checked with corpus.py page.
